name: 3d-scene-schema
summary: Engine-independent scene specification: the shared structure for scenes, objects, transforms, materials, assets, and metadata.
purpose: The source of truth for a 3D scene. It is the shared contract between Unity, future Unreal Engine apps, web applications, AI systems, geometry services, and APIs, so one scene can feed every runtime without rewriting the format.
install: This repository holds JSON Schema (2020-12) files rather than an installable package. Read schema/v1/ and the examples/ folder in the repository, or use an engine adapter such as 3d-unity-scene.
usage: Applications and engine adapters read and write scene documents that conform to the schema. Every document carries a schemaVersion (semver); breaking changes get a new schema/v{n}/ directory instead of changing v1. Units are meters in a right-handed, Y-up system, and engine adapters convert to and from their own conventions.
current: scene.schema.json: root document with schemaVersion, sceneId, timestamps, units, origin, and a flat list of objects
scene-object.schema.json: a semantic label (ROOM, FLOOR, CEILING, WALL_FACE, DOOR_FRAME, WINDOW_FRAME and common furniture), a transform, an optional boundary or volume, and a parentId
transform.schema.json and common.schema.json: position, rotation, scale, and shared primitives
features: Semantic labels that mirror Meta Quest Scene API / MRUK classifications
A per-scene origin so several scenes can share one coordinate frame
examples: A scanned room described as one scene
A corridor scan sharing a coordinate frame with a room scan

name: 3d-unity-core
summary: Core runtime package of the IT-Kamianets 3D Engine: shared Unity systems, configuration, utilities, and base architecture.
purpose: The foundation for Unity applications built on the engine. It holds shared runtime infrastructure that the other Unity packages depend on, and it stays product-independent with no game-specific functionality.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-core.git
usage: It acts as the common base for the Unity packages: 3d-unity-scene, 3d-unity-assets, 3d-unity-interaction, 3d-unity-xr, and 3d-unity-spatial. Its responsibility is common configuration, services, lifecycle handling, events, utilities, logging, dependency access, and shared runtime abstractions.
current: Standard UPM layout: package.json, Runtime/, Editor/, and Tests/ with assembly definitions
No runtime code yet; the package is installable and referenceable by the other Unity packages
features: Product-independent base for every Unity package
examples: Declared as a dependency by 3d-unity-scene, 3d-unity-xr, and 3d-unity-spatial

name: 3d-unity-scene
summary: Scene runtime package: loads, saves, synchronizes, and rebuilds 3D scenes in Unity from the shared scene schema.
purpose: It converts engine-independent scene definitions into live Unity scenes and synchronizes changes back into the shared scene format, so Unity is never the permanent source of truth.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-scene.git. It also uses com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json 3.2.1.
usage: The package sits between Unity and 3d-scene-schema: Scene Schema → Unity Scene → Scene Changes → Scene Schema. Use SceneJson to convert the C# scene data model to and from the schema's JSON.
current: A C# data model of 3d-scene-schema v1 under Runtime/Model/
SceneJson for converting the model to and from the schema's JSON (Newtonsoft.Json, with field names mapped to the schema)
Not built yet: instantiating a live Unity scene from SceneData, and syncing edits back out
features: C# data model of the scene schema v1
JSON conversion matching the schema's camelCase field names
Designed so the shared scene format can also serve Unreal, web viewers, and AI tools
examples: A Quest room scan converted to SceneData, then to JSON for upload

name: 3d-unity-assets
summary: Asset management package: 3D models, materials, textures, metadata, and runtime asset loading.
purpose: It discovers, loads, caches, and manages the 3D assets used by engine scenes. Scenes reference assets instead of embedding Unity-specific objects, and this package decides how an asset such as a chair, vehicle, tree, or wall module is loaded into Unity.
install: Not installable yet: the repository currently contains only a README and a license. Installation instructions will appear here once the Unity package is published.
usage: It is the bridge between asset metadata and actual Unity runtime objects: a scene object references an asset by ID, and this package resolves it.
current: README and roadmap only; no package code yet
examples: Resolving the model for an object that references a chair asset

name: 3d-unity-interaction
summary: Object editing package: selection, movement, rotation, scaling, snapping, duplication, and deletion.
purpose: It provides reusable 3D editing and object manipulation so applications can modify their scenes interactively without building editing tools for every product. It exposes generic operations, so the same system serves interiors, game levels, racing tracks, and simulations.
install: Not installable yet: the repository currently contains only a README and a license. Installation instructions will appear here once the Unity package is published.
usage: It operates on objects managed by 3d-unity-scene and keeps editing changes in sync with the scene.
current: README and roadmap only; no package code yet
features: Move, rotate, scale, duplicate, and delete
Grid, object, surface, and rotation snapping
examples: Moving and snapping furniture in a scanned room
Editing objects in a game level

name: 3d-unity-xr
summary: XR package: Meta Quest / VR interaction, controllers, hand tracking, locomotion, and XR tools.
purpose: It brings the engine's generic interaction capabilities into VR and MR, handling how users interact with a 3D world through XR. The initial target is Meta Quest, and the architecture is meant to suit other XR platforms later. Room scanning and physical-room understanding belong to 3d-unity-spatial.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-xr.git. It also uses com.unity.textmeshpro 3.0.6.
usage: Add it to a Quest project. XRPrimaryButtonAction fires once per controller button press without knowing what the button does, and StatusHud shows world-space text through SetStatus(string) without knowing what it reports on.
current: XRPrimaryButtonAction: fires once per controller button press
Not built yet: hand tracking, grabbing, teleportation, locomotion, and XR UI
features: Meta Quest first, other XR platforms later
examples: Triggering a room scan with a controller button and showing progress in a HUD

name: 3d-unity-spatial
summary: Spatial computing package: room scanning, spatial anchors, boundaries, surfaces, and real-world environment mapping.
purpose: It connects the engine with real physical environments: room understanding, physical surfaces, boundaries, anchors, and environment scanning. Where 3d-unity-xr handles XR hardware, this package understands the physical space around the user and converts it into engine-independent scene data.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-spatial.git. Install the Meta XR MR Utility Kit (com.meta.xr.mrutilitykit) in your project too; without it the package compiles to a no-op and ScanFailed fires with an explanatory message.
usage: RoomScanner requests the Quest Scene API permission, loads the current room through MR Utility Kit, and converts it into a SceneData from 3d-unity-scene. One MRUKRoom becomes one SceneData.
current: RoomScanner: Quest Scene API permission, MRUK room loading, and conversion to SceneData
Scan and upload only: no multi-room splitting, rescan/compare, or loading a SceneData back into MRUK
Written against the documented MRUK API and not yet verified against a live SDK version, so member names may need adjusting
features: Meta Quest Scene API and MRUK integration
One scanned room converted to one scene
Graceful no-op when MRUK is not installed
examples: Turning a real room into the initial digital scene for VRoom
roadmap: Alignment between virtual and physical scenes
